title: Choose the dashboard structure
question: Which home screen would make it easiest to decide what to study next?

options.label: Study Itinerary
options.thesis: Turn the day into one legible route from now, through the next deadline, to the next study move.
options.viewport: A wide Today route dominates the left two thirds; the current study action is a dark focal block, while deadlines and course readiness form a quiet right rail.
options.risk: The route needs a convincing empty-day state when no timetable is connected.

options.label: Focus Command
options.thesis: Make one recommended study action the unmistakable center, with every metric demoted to supporting evidence.
options.viewport: A single elevated focus plane holds the recommended course, reason, and start action; a slim week strip sits above and two terse ledgers sit below.
options.risk: A recommendation can feel invented when the account has too little activity data.

options.label: Split Horizon
options.thesis: Put immediate pressure and degree readiness side by side so today never obscures the larger exam trajectory.
options.viewport: The left side is a compact Today agenda and start action; the right side is a course-by-course readiness matrix with exam distance, reading progress, and weak-work signals.
options.risk: The matrix can become too analytical for a quick morning check.
